CFML Language Reference: Functions

Exp

Returns the constant e (2.71828182846, the base of natural logarithms) raised to the given power.

Category

Mathematical functions

Syntax

Exp(number)

Parameters

number
The exponent.

Returns

A positive number.

Usage

Exp is the inverse of Log: Log(Exp(x)) is x. For other bases use the ^ operator, for example 2^10. Compound interest calculated continuously is Principal * Exp(Rate * Years).

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>number</TH><TH>Exp(number)</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="n" LIST="0,1,2,-1,10">
<CFOUTPUT><TR><TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#n#</TD><TD>#Exp(n)#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>$1,000 at 5% compounded continuously for 10 years:
#DollarFormat(1000 * Exp(0.05 * 10))#
</CFOUTPUT>
